description: Chandragupta to Ashoka, Arthashastra, four-tier administration, espionage, decline

questions.stem: The Mauryan Empire was founded in c. 322 BCE by:

options.option_text: Chandragupta Maurya (with help of his guru Kautilya / Chanakya)

questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya — overthrew the last Nanda ruler Dhana Nanda c. 322 BCE with strategic guidance from his guru Kautilya / Chanakya / Vishnugupta. Defeated Seleucus I Nicator (323 BCE) — Greek general, who ceded Hindu Kush territories in exchange for 500 elephants and a treaty. Greek ambassador Megasthenes visited Chandragupta's court at Pataliputra (~302 BCE) and wrote 'Indica' (only fragments survive). Chandragupta later abdicated (~298 BCE) → became a Jain monk under Bhadrabahu, fasted to death at Shravanabelagola, Karnataka.

options.option_text: A treatise on statecraft, economics, and military strategy

questions.explanation: Arthashastra — composed by Kautilya / Chanakya — practical handbook of statecraft (kingship, taxation, espionage, foreign policy, war), economics, law. ~6,000 sutras across 15 'adhikaranas' (books). Discusses 'saptanga' theory (7 organs of state — Swami/king, Amatya/minister, Janapada/territory+population, Durga/fort, Kosha/treasury, Danda/army, Mitra/ally). Also defines 'mandala' theory of foreign policy — 'enemy of my enemy is my friend'. Rediscovered 1905 by R. Shamasastry (Mysore). Some scholars argue final form is post-Kautilya (1st-2nd C CE).

questions.stem: The capital of the Mauryan Empire was:

options.option_text: Pataliputra (modern Patna, Bihar) — at confluence of Ganga, Son, Gandak

questions.explanation: Pataliputra — fortified city on the south bank of Ganga, with Son flowing on one side and Gandak across. Founded by Ajatashatru (Magadha king, ~5th C BCE), capital of Magadha continuously through the Mauryan Empire. Megasthenes described it as 'Palibothra' — 14.5 × 2.5 km, surrounded by deep moat + 570 towers + 64 gates. Other major Mauryan cities: Taxila (NW capital — major centre of learning), Ujjain (administrative HQ for west), Suvarnagiri (south HQ), Tosali (east).

questions.stem: Ashoka the Great (r. 268-232 BCE) embraced Buddhism after the:
questions.explanation: Kalinga War (~261 BCE) — Ashoka conquered Kalinga (modern Odisha + parts of AP) at huge human cost (per his own Edict 13, ~150,000 deported, 100,000 killed, many more died). Witnessing the carnage led to his conversion to Buddhism, embrace of 'dhamma vijaya' (conquest by righteousness, not war). His Rock Edicts XIII, IX, X describe these. Adopted 'Devanampriya Priyadarsi' as his epithet. Sent missions to Sri Lanka (his son Mahinda + daughter Sanghamitra), Greek kingdoms (Antiochus II, Ptolemy II), Burma, Thailand.

questions.stem: The Mauryan Empire used a sophisticated SPY SYSTEM. According to Arthashastra, two main classes of spies were:
questions.explanation: Kautilya's espionage system — extensive. Sansthana spies — embedded permanently in their cover identity (a 'fraudulent disciple', 'recluse with pupils', 'secret agent at the court', 'merchant agent'). Sanchara spies — itinerant, on 'special missions' (snake charmer, magician, bard). Used to surveil ministers, queens, princes, foreign emissaries, commoners, even the king himself. Reports cross-checked across multiple agents. Reflective of the 'security state' approach Kautilya advocated. Megasthenes (Indica) corroborates an extensive royal spy network.

questions.stem: The Lion Capital of Sarnath — adopted as India's national emblem — depicts how many lions standing back-to-back?

options.option_text: Four (one always hidden from any single viewing angle)

questions.explanation: Lion Capital — top of an Ashokan pillar at Sarnath, near Varanasi. FOUR lions, back to back facing the four cardinal directions. Below them — four animals (elephant, bull, horse, lion) and four Dharma Chakras. Above an inverted lotus base. Adopted as India's National Emblem on 26 January 1950. The motto 'Satyameva Jayate' (truth alone triumphs) below — from Mundaka Upanishad. From any one angle only 3 lions are visible; the 4th is hidden behind. New emblem version unveiled atop the new Parliament building in 2022 was controversial — some accused that the lions look more 'aggressive'.

questions.stem: The last Mauryan emperor, Brihadratha, was killed in c. 185 BCE, ending the Mauryan dynasty. He was assassinated by:

options.option_text: Pushyamitra Shunga, his commander-in-chief — founder of the Shunga dynasty

questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga — Brahmin general of Brihadratha. Killed his own emperor during a military review at Pataliputra (~185 BCE). Founded the Shunga dynasty (185-73 BCE), ruled Magadha for ~36 years. Patronised Sanskrit revival; performed Ashvamedha sacrifices (a turn from Mauryan Buddhist patronage). Some Buddhist sources accuse him of persecuting Buddhists; modern historians question this. Decline of Mauryan empire — multiple causes: vast empire, weak successors after Ashoka, financial strain, emergent local satraps.
